resolutions.researcher_notes: Brief confirms the wiki's '30/36 inches' string flagged as 'Capacity' is a misparsed diameter, not a capacity value, so nothing is staged from it. Searched offshore-technology.com and nsenergybusiness.com (both have a dedicated market-data profile for the Wafa-Mellitah line but none for Defa-Brega), the 2024 OPEC Annual Statistical Bulletin (downloaded and pdftotext'd asb-2024.pdf directly from opec.org, which resolved fine this session -- no Table 4.10-style gas-pipeline listing exists in this edition at all, and neither 'Defa' nor 'Brega' appear near any pipeline table), and Wikipedia (Raguba field, Zelten oil field -- both only describe a Zelten/Raguba-Brega OIL pipeline via Nasser field, not this gas line, and cite no operational specs). Gem.wiki's own single citation for this page is 'World Energy Atlas, Petroleum Economist, 2001' -- a print atlas, not a fetchable/verifiable URL, and not usable as a ref per protocol anyway. No independent diameter or capacity figure for the actual Defa-Brega Gas Pipeline was found. UNRESOLVED.

No commissioning-year source found for this specific pipeline. Defa oil/gas field was discovered by 1962 and is a long-producing Sirte Basin field, so the gas line is plausibly a 1970s-80s vintage gathering/trunk line, but I found no source that dates the pipeline itself (as opposed to the field). Did not find any Defa-Brega-specific coverage in Libya Herald/Libya Observer/Zawya archives (those cover the newer 2026 Farigh-Brega line, a different, later pipeline that ties into the same 42-inch Sirte Oil Company trunk network at Brega). UNRESOLVED.

The wiki's suggested 'Libya National Oil Corporation' for Operator conflates Owner and Operator -- a recurring pattern this protocol flags for Libya rows (NOC is the owner, one of its joint-venture operating companies is the operator). I did not cite the wiki; I verified independently. The live opec.org original of OPEC's Annual Statistical Bulletin 2012 is dead (known batch gotcha, redirects to homepage); I recovered the 2012-07-22 Wayback capture myself (curl 200, CDX-confirmed) and ran pdftotext -layout on the full PDF directly. Table 4.10 'Gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2011' (printed p.75), Libya section, lists ALL FOUR segments making up this aggregate route with the SAME named operator: 'Brega/Benghazi Sirte Oil 246 34 10,761,824 na', 'Brega/Khoms Sirte Oil 645 34 11,611,442 na', 'Khoms/Tripoli Sirte Oil 125 34 17,048,995 na', 'Tripoli/Mellitah Sirte Oil 98 34 16,992,353 na' -- i.e. Sirte Oil Co, not NOC directly, is OPEC's own recorded operator of every constituent stretch of this aggregate corridor. Independently, Wikipedia's National Oil Corporation article (verified live) lists Sirte Oil Company (SOC) among NOC's subsidiaries, and NOC's own official site (noc.ly, verified live, Arabic, contains 'Sirte') lists 'Sirte Oil Company' among its affiliated companies -- both confirming SOC is NOC's wholly-owned operating subsidiary, consistent with the sheet's existing Owner1=Libyan National Oil Corp at 100%, while Operator should read Sirte Oil Co specifically. Two independent origins (an OPEC/industry statistics body naming the operator segment-by-segment, and NOC's own corporate-structure sources) triangulate on the same operator; tier high.

The route's length_ratio flag is already staged elsewhere (redundancy cluster B, the 5246 km value is a decimal-shift error against the drawn 526 km route) -- per brief context I only researched Operator here. Offshore-technology.com's dedicated market-data profile for this line states it is 'operated by Mellitah Oil & Gas', a 525 km onshore pipeline, max diameter 32in, started 2004, ending at Nuqat Al-Khams (i.e. the Mellitah complex) -- all consistent with the sheet's own values (Diameter=32, StartYear1=2004). Independently, Mellitah Oil & Gas's own site (Company Achievements page) describes 'a 525 km network with 32in gas and 16in oil/condensates pipelines running parallel from Wafa Desert to Mellitah (completed August 2004)' as part of its own operated infrastructure -- a primary-source confirmation from a wholly separate origin (the operating company itself vs. a GlobalData trade profile), giving independent corroboration and a high tier.

Punj Lloyd's own 25-years retrospective (Yumpu-hosted company publication, p.56, verified live, contains 'Melita') states the government set a target for Punj Lloyd to commission the Tripoli-Melita gas pipeline early, 'charging gas from Melita to Zawia Power Plant by March 2010,' and that 'Punj Lloyd achieved this target.' A 2020 Libya Herald article (verified live, contains 'Punj Lloyd') on Sirte Oil's successful defense of an ICC arbitration brought by Punj Lloyd corroborates that Punj Lloyd built a Sirte-Oil-contracted gas pipeline in this corridor and that construction/completion was disrupted around the 2011 revolution period. Tier medium rather than high: the two sources are not fully independent in origin (Punj Lloyd's own retrospective is a primary-but-self-interested account; Libya Herald corroborates the contractor/project relationship and dispute but does not itself restate the March 2010 commissioning date). No second, fully independent outlet was found stating the exact 2010 date before WebSearch budget was exhausted for this session.

Traced the 333.00 km sheet value to a unit-conversion error in GEM's own underlying source (read as a lead only, not cited): gem.wiki cites OPEC ASB2012 Table 4.10 (2011 data), which lists 'Intesar/Brega, Zueitina, 207, 42in, 42,480,884' under a column literally headed 'Length (miles)'. I recovered the dead opec.org PDF via Wayback (https://web.archive.org/web/20250110032615/https://opec.org/.../ASB2012.pdf) and pdftotext-extracted Table 4.10 directly (url_verifier FAILs on this PDF because it does a plain-text substring check on the raw file and can't parse the PDF's compressed text streams -- a known false-negative, not proof of a dead/unsupported source; I manually confirmed the exact row text). The ASB2012 column header is provably mislabeled: cross-checking against ASB2013 (2012 data, same table), the Mellitah/Gela entry (the well-documented Greenstream subsea pipeline) reads '334.8' under the same 'miles' header, and 334.8 mi x 1.609 = 538.7 km, matching both ASB2012's raw '540' AND Wikipedia's authoritative Greenstream length of 540 km (verified live) -- proving ASB2012's raw numbers are ALREADY in km despite the mile header, while ASB2013's are genuine miles. Applying the same check to Intesar/Brega: ASB2013 gives 128.34 mi x 1.609 = 206.5 km, matching ASB2012's raw '207' almost exactly. So the true sourced length is ~207 km, and GEM appears to have taken that 207-km ASB figure and mis-converted it AGAIN as if it were miles (207 x 1.609 = 333.06 -> 333.00), doubling the error. Independent, non-OPEC confirmation: two MEED articles on the original construction tender (Sept 2005 'Chinese in front for Zueitina pipeline', and Jan 2006 'CPECC takes Zueitina pipeline', both verified live and containing '215') both describe 'construction of a 42-inch-diameter, 215-kilometre-long steel pipeline' from 'Zueitina's 103A supply base in the Sirte basin to the Brega coastal pipeline,' contractor CPECC. Zueitina Oil Company's own project page (gas-transfer-project-103-intisar-field-to-a-coastal-network) independently describes '207 kilometers from the 103 field to Brega' per search-engine indexing, but the live page is a JS single-page app that renders empty to any scraper/verifier (confirmed via curl: static HTML has no body text) -- treated as a corroborating lead only, not a citable ref. Net: three converging figures (ASB raw 207, ASB-miles-recomputed 206.5, Zueitina's own 207) plus MEED's independently reported 215 all cluster at ~207-215 km, closely matching the drawn route (223 km, ratio 223/215=1.04). Proposing LengthKnownKm=215 (MEED, the cleanest single citable figure) as the correction; the drawn route is approximately right and the sheet's 333 km is the error, not the geometry.

MEED (2005/2006, on the original pipeline construction contract) describes the line as running from 'Zueitina's 103A supply base'; Libya Herald (April 2026, on the recently completed connecting segment from Field 103 to Sirte Oil's Line 36B) explicitly attributes the works to Zueitina Oil Company under NOC. Both independently name Zueitina Oil Co as the operating entity for this Field-103/Intisar corridor, consistent with the sheet's existing (currently unreferenced) Operator value -- no change to the value, just adding refs. Note: a large new 42-inch, 130 km segment from Zueitina's Field 103 to Sirte Oil's Line 36B (also reported as the 'Farigh-Brega Gas Pipeline') was completed/trial-commissioned in April 2026 after being stalled since before 2011; this is very likely a related but distinct newer segment/expansion in the same corridor, not necessarily identical to the pipeline this GEM row represents -- flagged as a possible related-entity question for a human to consider (see validity note), not resolved here since it is outside the length_ratio flag this row was assigned.

Could not find a sourced commissioning year for this specific internal 41 km/40in gas line between fields 103D and 103A (both in Zueitina Oil Co's Sirte-basin concession 103). What IS established: field 103 (Intisar/Idris) was discovered by Occidental in late 1967, with a 40-inch OIL export pipeline to Zueitina terminal built/operating by February 1968 (AAPG Explorer 'The Oil Hunters of Libya', verified live; OSTI biblio/6090661 on Occidental's Libyan gas-reinjection operations, verified/fetched). Critically, that OSTI paper describes the ORIGINAL 1968-era design as reinjecting associated gas back into the reservoir for pressure maintenance rather than piping it to shore -- meaning the gas-gathering pipelines (like this 103D-103A line) were very likely a later addition once gas began being piped/sold rather than reinjected, not contemporaneous with the 1968 oil buildout. Per the protocol, a field's first-production year is not automatically its pipeline's commissioning year, and I am treating the 1968 date as exactly that kind of non-answer -- flagging it, not using it. The only firm anchor I have is a upper bound: OPEC ASB Table 4.10 (2011 data, recovered from Wayback + pdftotext per the protocol's known gotcha) already lists '103D/103A, Zueitina, ...' as an existing, operating, capacity-reporting line in 2011, so it was commissioned no later than 2011. No dated news article, company history, or trade-press piece naming an actual construction/commissioning year for this specific segment turned up before the session's WebSearch budget was exhausted. Marking UNRESOLVED rather than guessing.

MEED (2005 construction-tender article, verified live) describes 'Zueitina's 103A supply base in the Sirte basin', confirming Zueitina Oil Co as the operator of the field-103/103A infrastructure this internal gas line sits within, consistent with the sheet's existing (currently unreferenced) Operator value. Tier medium rather than high: this MEED mention is about the broader Field-103A supply-base project, not a citation naming the specific 103D-103A segment by name, and I could not find a second, fully independent source that names this exact 41 km internal line. OPEC ASB2012 Table 4.10 also lists '103D/103A' under owner/operator 'Zueitina' (same recovered-PDF source used for the length observation below), but I am not double-counting it as a second independent source here since it is the same underlying document family already cited for P1856/the length flag on this cluster.

Mellitah Oil & Gas's own tender portal (verified live, contains 'Attifel') is soliciting bids to replace 'the Launching & Receiving Traps of the 34" Gas Line at ABU-ATTIFEL Field (A100/103 A)' -- a direct, primary-source confirmation that Mellitah Oil & Gas operates the 34-inch Bu-Attifel gas line. OPEC ASB Table 4.10 (2011 data; PDF dead on the live opec.org site, recovered via Wayback per the protocol's known gotcha and confirmed by pdftotext -- url_verifier's substring check FAILs on the raw PDF bytes, a known false-negative for PDF content, so I manually verified) independently lists 'Bu-Attifel/Intesar, Mellitah Oil and Gas, 133, 34in, 11,328,236', agreeing with the sheet's existing (currently unreferenced) Operator value. Two independent origins (Mellitah's own site; OPEC's intergovernmental compilation) -- tier high.

The sheet's 177.00 km is the same double-conversion bug found on P1856/P1857 in this cluster. OPEC ASB Table 4.10 (opec.org PDFs dead on the live site; recovered via Wayback + pdftotext per the protocol's gotcha; url_verifier FAILs on both PDFs because it can't substring-match compressed PDF text streams -- a known false-negative, manually confirmed by me) lists: ASB2012 (2011 data) 'Waha/Nasser, Waha, 110, 24in, 5,664,118' under a column headed '(miles)'; ASB2013 (2012 data) restates the same route as '68.2' under a column that IS genuine miles (68.2 x 1.609 = 109.75 km, matching ASB2012's raw '110' almost exactly). As established on P1856 (using the well-documented 540 km Greenstream pipeline in the same table as ground truth), ASB2012's 'miles' header is mislabeled -- those values are already in km. So the true sourced length is ~110 km, and the sheet's 177.00 km = 110 x 1.609, i.e. GEM re-applied a miles-to-km conversion to a value that was already in km. Proposing LengthKnownKm=110. Note the drawn route (69.9 km) is still short of even the corrected 110 km (ratio 0.64, still below the 0.75 tolerance floor) -- closer than the 0.39 ratio against 177 km, but not fully resolved; recommend the route also be reviewed (see validity note) even though the length fix is the primary and better-evidenced correction.

Ecofin Agency (Dec 2025, verified live, contains 'Waha') confirms Waha Oil Company -- a joint venture of NOC, TotalEnergies and ConocoPhillips, matching the sheet's Owner field exactly -- operates the Farigh/Nasser Sirte-basin gas fields this line serves. OPEC ASB Table 4.10 (same recovered-PDF source cited for the length fill above) independently lists owner/operator 'Waha' for the Waha/Nasser route, corroborating the value, but I'm not double-counting that as a second independent source here since it's the same document family already cited for the length fix on this row. Tier medium: one genuinely distinct non-OPEC source found and verified before the session's WebSearch budget was exhausted.

No sourced commissioning year found for this specific gas line. OPEC ASB Table 4.10 (2011 data, recovered via Wayback + pdftotext) already lists 'Waha/Nasser' as an existing, operating, capacity-reporting line by end-2011, so it was commissioned no later than 2011 -- an upper bound only, not an answer.
